BY ADV SRI.VPK.PANICKER  THIS CROSS OBJECTION/CROSS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 06.02.2025, ALONG WITH MACA.2271/2016, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO.2271 OF 2016 & CO NO.118 OF 2016 3 2025:KER:13214  JUDGMENT Dated this the 06th day of February, 2025.

The respondent No.3 in O.P.(M.V.) No.752/ 2013 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Pala is the appellant herein.
Petitioners in the above OP are the cross-objectors.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)

2. The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the legal representatives of the deceased by name Lalumon, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 20.04.2013.

According to them, on 20.04.2013, at about 10.40 a.m, while the deceased was riding a motorcycle from Punchavayal to Mundakayam, a stage carriage bearing registration No.KL-05/S-4713 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motcycle of the deceased and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries and later on he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner , the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle. According to MACA NO.2271 OF 2016 & CO NO.118 OF 2016 4 2025:KER:13214 the petitioners
, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was Rs.32,97,000/- and is limited to Rs.32,00,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PW's 1 and 2, RW1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A13 and Ext.B1.

sentences.text: After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.19,23,000/-.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the 3rd respondent has preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
9. Heard Sri.V.P.K. Panicker, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Appellant, and Sri.Mathew K. Philip, the learned Counsel for the respondents/ cross- objectors.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as validity policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent is regarding the income of the deceased as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was working as Marketing Manager, earning Rs.15,000/- per month, and the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.10,000/-.
11. The Tribunal found that the petitioners could not prove the job or income of the deceased.
Even then, the notional income of the deceased was taken as Rs.10000/-.

Since the petitioners could not prove the job or income of the deceased as claimed in the OP, in the light of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.9,000/-.
12.

Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

Since the deceased was married who left behind 5 dependants, towards personal and living expense, 1/4 of the income is MACA NO.2271 OF 2016 &
CO NO.118 OF 2016 6 2025:KER:13214 liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).
In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.15,75,000/-.
13. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.1,000,00/- towards loss of consortium and Rs. 75,000/- towards love and affection.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15000/- towards funeral expenses, and each dependent is entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.
Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense

14. Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.

Therefore, the petitioners/ appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.18,88,300/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

 6 Loss of love and affection 75,000/- Nil  7 Loss of consortium 1,00,000/- 2,42,000/-
 Total 19,23,000/- 18,88,300/-

17.

The Tribunal found 20% negligence on the part of the deceased on the ground that before the accident he overtook an autorickshaw and that as per the scene mahazar, the motorcycle went beyond the midline of the road.
The law is well settled that for the mere reason that before the accident the deceased overtook an autorickshaw, no negligence can be attributed against the deceased.
The person who prepared the scene mahazar was also not examined to prove the same.
In the above circumstance, the finding of the Tribunal that there was 20% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased is liable to be set aside and I do accordingly.
